title: Observation, Evidence, Proof and Truth Surfaces
results: Reality, Fact, Claim, Observation, Record, Evidence, Proof and Projection are distinct.
Observation is observer/method/scope/time-relative and a correct observation can be insufficient for a broader claim.
Evidence is claim-relative and proof additionally requires a declared contract/inference.
Truth-owner language is refined to fact-scoped canonical commit/reconstruction authority under a named contract rather than ownership of Reality itself.
Current Runtime remains correctly federated across Git/filesystem, SQLite Registry, systemd/cgroup, Windows process ownership, Runner evidence, structured Effect receipts and Host/domain authorities.
Provenance, authenticity, integrity, semantic correctness, completeness and freshness are independent evidence dimensions.
Cryptographic digests establish byte identity/change relationships but do not establish provenance, authority or semantic validity.
Digital signatures establish origin/integrity properties under key/trust assumptions but do not prove arbitrary signed claims true.
Timestamps, generations and row versions establish only the time/order/freshness relations their owner contracts define.
Identity binding is central to evidence strength and unbound plausible logs/results cannot safely identify an Operation/process.
Direct/domain evidence differs from derived projections even though direct evidence still requires validation.
Projection correctness and completeness are orthogonal; bounded correct lists can remain incomplete.
Current truncation flags/cursors are epistemically significant and must block closed-set inference when incomplete.
SQLite query snapshots provide owner-local Registry consistency rather than a global snapshot across Git/filesystem/process/external owners.
Cross-owner global state requires an explicit snapshot/reconciliation protocol rather than arbitrary multi-source reads.
Freshness is claim-relative and stale evidence may remain historically correct.
Evidence precedence is claim-specific and newer records are not automatically stronger.
Terminal-evidence supersession correctly allows stronger late evidence to revise current conclusions without erasing prior evidence history.
Corroboration requires independent provenance/failure domains; multiple projections of one source are not independent evidence.
Absence of observation is not proof of absence without completeness/timing/substrate assumptions.
Windows KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE enables stronger negative process evidence than generic Linux absence because the substrate contract eliminates more alternatives.
P4 proves no host inotify/path drift is not target-byte-consumption proof; scope runtime_host_namespace_path_witness remains correct.
Receipts are authoritative only for transitions/effects their issuer/domain actually owns; Release receipt may be stronger than process state for deployment Effect claims.
Artifact existence/digest/truncation proves retained evidence bytes and completeness limits rather than semantic correctness.
Generic scalar confidence is unjustified for deterministic Runtime mechanical claims without a calibrated probabilistic model.
Evidence custodianship does not confer issuer/domain authority for the underlying fact.

Preferred Runtime epistemic architecture is federated scoped authority plus identity-bound evidence plus explicit provenance/integrity/completeness/freshness boundaries plus claim-directed reconciliation rather than a synthetic global truth database.

nextRound.title: Composition, Transactions and Cross-Operation Atomicity
nextRound.entryQuestion: When several Operations/effects compose, which owner can truthfully provide atomic commit, where do partial commit and distributed uncertainty appear, and when is the right model orchestration or compensation rather than transactionality?

notes: RF11 refines evidence/truth language but does not authorize a new evidence database, provenance graph, signatures, confidence scores, global snapshot layer or production API changes.
